purpose: Teach: コイツ/フラフラ/おととい/がまん/ちょこちょこ/まちまち/何時も/物凄く

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは仲間を「コイツが頼りだ」って言われたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, people used to say about him, "That's the guy you can count on."
lines.style: Soft, distant memory. Slow pace with a gentle beat on the key image. Voice settles into warmth—not sad, but tender with time. Slight pause before speaking, like reaching back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、夏祭りの後、フラフラなさってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and Grandpa, after the summer festival you could barely stand, couldn't you?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate teasing. Gentle lilt on the observation—she's seen this before. Familiar rhythm, like they've danced this many times. A soft chuckle underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、おとといお孫さんがお見えになったのを覚えてるぞ
lines.en: Gran, do you remember when our grandson came to visit the other day?
lines.style: Quieter now, more deliberate. Testing her memory gently—not pushing, but reaching. Voice softens on the question. The care underneath is obvious but never stated.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、つらい時もがまんなさってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, even when times were hard you never complained, did you?
lines.style: Recognition in her voice—she knows his strength. Soft, almost reverent. Not a question that needs answering; a statement of knowing. Warm exhale at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがちょこちょこお見えになったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to visit us so often.
lines.style: Measured, like placing a memory down carefully. Each phrase has space around it. Voice is steady, almost wondering at how vivid it still is. No rush.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご友人のご出身がまちまちで楽しい集まりだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, your gatherings were always so lively with friends from all different places, weren't they?
lines.style: Bright recollection, a smile in her voice. Energy picks up slightly—she's seeing the room again. Warm, genuine delight in remembering the life they built together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは何時も静かに笑ってらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he always had that quiet smile on his face.
lines.style: Most tender yet. Voice drops slightly, almost reverent. Long, gentle pauses between phrases. Like he's describing something sacred—the way someone loved. Exhale at the end, letting it rest.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、孫の成長を物凄く喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you were so incredibly happy whenever our grandchildren grew and changed, weren't you?
lines.style: Gentle warmth with recognition of a lifetime. Voice is soft but full—she's seen him light up with this joy. Trailing words fade like a satisfied sigh, close to his ear.
